chunks: Thirteen - Muhammad ibn Uthman narrated, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Raqqi narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Mujalid ibn Sa'id, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said:'

We were with Ibn Mas'ood, and a man asked him: 'Has your Prophet told you how many caliphs will be after him?' He said: 'Yes, and no one has asked me about it before you, for you are the youngest of the people in age. I heard him saying: After me, there will be (as many) as the number of the chieftains of Moses (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: How many caliphs will follow the Prophet according to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ood?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Ibn Mas'ud, records the Prophet Muhammad's prediction that his successors would number twelve, explicitly comparing them to the twelve chieftains (nuqaba') appointed by Moses. In Shia scholarship, this is a foundational proof for the Imamate of the Twelve Imams, emphasizing divine appointment and the continuity of prophetic leadership through a specific, divinely ordained number.
